'''Torricelli''' is a [[Lunar craters|lunar]] [[impact crater]] in the eastern part of the [[Sinus Asperitatis]], to the south of the [[Mare Tranquillitatis]]. It was named after Italian physicist [[Evangelista Torricelli]].<ref>{{gpn|6065}}</ref> The western rim of the crater is broken open and joined to a smaller crater to the west. The entire formation has a pear-shaped appearance. Torricelli lies in the northeastern part of a circular formation of rises in the [[lunar mare]], possibly the remains of a crater formation buried by [[lava]].

==Satellite craters==
By convention these features are identified on lunar maps by placing the letter on the side of the crater midpoint that is closest to Torricelli.
